text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Some 100,000 people demonstrate in Belgrade over annullment of local election results in sixth day of protests.
- Demonstrations over election annullments were also held in Nis, Uzice, Kraljevo and other Serbian towns.
- The opposition coalition Zajedno appeals to Serbia's Supreme Court over decision of the municipal court to annul opposition victory in Belgrade.
- The Yugoslav federal government to decide on Thursday whether to set import quota of 300,000 tonnes of wheat.
- Trade union of Kolubara mines protests over difficult working conditions.

- Yugoslavia's 1997 economic policy goal of maintaining stability of prices and currency, increase of production, exports and standard of living have been adjusted between federal and republican governments, says Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic.

- Yugoslavia and France should confirm earlier agreements such as an agreement on avoidance of double taxation and protection of investment says President of Yugoslav Chamber of Economy Mihajlo Milojevic.
- Domestic cigarette prices go up by 30 percent on average.
- Serbia expects to produce 280,000 tonnes of sugar this year.

- Yugoslav railways and Greek-German joint stock freight forwarding company Prodos sign an agreement in Belgrade on the transit of goods going from northern and western Europe to the south and east through Yugoslavia.
- The Serbian oil industry NIS of Novi Sad and London RDS Oilfield Services Ltd sign in London an agreement on forming a joint stock company.
- Third round of Serbian local elections will be held on Wednesday, November 27 in 232 polling stations.

- The ship Galeb, which used to be the state ship of late Yugoslav president Josip Broz Tito, is still waiting for a buyer in a Montenegrin port at daily costs of one thousand dollars. The price of the vessel is set at 3 mllion German marks.
- Yugoslav firms start to recycle waste, with the steel works Sartid 1913 and tyre factory Trajal among the first to process waste materials. -- Belgrade newsroom, 381 11 222 425
